rubric_rules: Safety risk must strictly outweigh public inconvenience.
Imminent danger to human life, live electricity, or open falls always warrant Critical priority.
Proximity to sensitive zones (schools, hospitals, busy transit corridors) escalates severity by one level.
Purely cosmetic or non-functional aesthetic defects must be classified as Low.

Critical.definition: Immediate, acute threat to human life, severe bodily harm, or catastrophic systemic failure requiring emergency intervention within 1 to 2 hours.
triggers: Exposed live high-voltage electric wires or sparking transformers near pedestrian reach
Open, missing, or broken manhole covers on active roads or walkways
Major water main burst causing road cave-in or structural foundation undermining
Fallen heavy tree or pole completely blocking arterial road or emergency vehicle access
Toxic chemical release, gas leak, or hazardous waste spill
Imminent wall or structure collapse over public right of way

High.definition: Substantial danger to public health and safety, severe property damage risk, or major disruption to essential civic services.
triggers: Deep crater potholes on high-speed or arterial roads causing two-wheeler accidents
Raw sewage backflow entering residential homes, schools, or healthcare facilities
Large fractured tree branch hanging precariously over power lines or busy footpaths
Prolonged total power outage affecting an entire ward or neighborhood
Pack of aggressive, biting stray dogs near schools, parks, or residential gates
Severe water contamination with foul smell and discolored drinking water supply
Blocked stormwater drain causing knee-deep road waterlogging during monsoon

Medium.definition: Noticeable civic inconvenience, localized hygiene issues, or moderate maintenance failures without immediate threat to life.
triggers: Overflowing municipal waste bin or uncollected garbage pile for 2-3 days
Non-working streetlights across a residential lane or colony stretch
Continuous minor roadside potable water pipeline leakage or dripping valve
Commercial footpath encroachment forcing pedestrians onto the road shoulder
Excessive construction noise during permitted daytime hours or unauthorized dust
Damaged speed breaker or broken pedestrian guardrail

Low.definition: Minor cosmetic, aesthetic, or routine non-urgent maintenance issues with negligible safety impact.
triggers: Faded zebra crossing or road line markings
Small roadside litter or dry leaf pile awaiting scheduled sweep
Graffiti or unauthorized posters on public municipal walls
Broken or weathered public park bench
Hairline cracks on footpath tiles with no tripping hazard
Minor park garden weeding or ornamental tree pruning
